s1.syndrome_frame: Gradual-onset unilateral facial weakness with a mass in the ear canal and abnormal imaging findings of the temporal bone
salient_findings: Nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal
Irregular lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen with heterogeneous enhancement on MRI
key_facts: 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness
Initially treated with oral steroids
No hearing loss, tinnitus, imbalance, or other cranial nerve deficits
Nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal
Mild sensorineural loss at 4000 Hz on audiographic findings
MRI showed a 5 × 10-mm irregular lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen
Lesion had heterogeneous enhancement on T1 with contrast
Follow-up MRI showed heterogeneous signal in the stylomastoid foramen on T2 images
CT showed expansion of the fallopian canal distal to the second genu of the facial nerve
Erosion of the posterior external auditory canal
Expansion of the stylomastoid foramen

shortlist: Low-grade chondrosarcoma of the temporal bone

shortlist.label: Chondrosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging findings of a heterogeneous lesion in the mastoid with expansion of the stylomastoid foramen and erosion of the posterior external auditory canal, along with microscopic examination showing pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei and positive S100 staining

shortlist.label: Facial nerve schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Gradual-onset unilateral facial weakness and a nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal, which could be consistent with a schwannoma involving the facial nerve

shortlist.label: Low-grade chondrosarcoma of the temporal bone
shortlist.why_kept: Microscopic findings of low cellularity, low MIB-1 proliferation index, and positive S100 staining, which are consistent with a low-grade chondrosarcoma

shortlist.label: Chondroma
shortlist.why_kept: Gross examination showing a tan to brown, rubbery specimen with cartilage, and microscopic examination showing a myxochondroid matrix, which could be consistent with a chondroma

shortlist.label: Myxoid chondrosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Microscopic examination showing a myxochondroid matrix and pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei, which could be consistent with a myxoid chondrosarcoma

s4.champion: Low-grade chondrosarcoma of the temporal bone

raw.champion: Low-grade chondrosarcoma of the temporal bone
raw.rationale: The patient's 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness, nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal, and imaging findings of a lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen with heterogeneous enhancement on T1 with contrast are consistent with a low-grade chondrosarcoma. The pathology results showing pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei, staining positive for S100, and low cellularity also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Chondrosarcoma
rejected.why: Too broad, as the specific location and grade are not specified

rejected.label: Facial nerve schwannoma
rejected.why: Imaging and pathology findings do not support a diagnosis of schwannoma

rejected.label: Chondroma
rejected.why: Pathology findings show atypical pleomorphic nuclei, suggesting a more malignant process than a benign chondroma

rejected.label: Myxoid chondrosarcoma
rejected.why: Not supported by the pathology findings, which do not describe a myxoid matrix
